subject: geom_bar warning: position_stack requires constant width

messages.author: e68a1208f312170f
messages.subject: geom_bar warning: position_stack requires constant width
parts:
Hi All --

When we try to create a stacked barplot with many discrete X values (~600), we get a warning message:

Warning message: position_stack requires constant width: output may be incorrect

You might ask why on earth  we would want to do such a thing when individual data are lost. We are plotting haplotypes across many markers and this visualization greatly helps identify trends.

Is this warning a numerical precision problem?


To replicate:

hapCount=4
markerCount=600

set.seed(3893393)
fakeyData=data.frame(value =runif(markerCount* hapCount), markerPosition =paste("pos", rep(1: markerCount, hapCount), sep=""), haplotype=paste("hap", rep(1: hapCount, each= markerCount), sep=""))

ggplot(fakeyData, aes(x = markerPosition, y = value, fill= haplotype, color=haplotype)) + geom_bar(stat = "identity", position="stack")

I'm using ggplot2  0.9.3.1, R version 2.15.2 (2012-10-26) -- "Trick or Treat" and R.app GUI 1.53 (6443) x86_64-apple-darwin9.8.0.

Thanks!

H

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: geom_bar warning: position_stack requires constant width
parts:
Interesting... it looks like it gives that message when markerCount>128. I've filed an issue for it in the tracker:
https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/issues/779

The issue is with a function called zero_range() which we've found in the past doesn't always do quite the right thing. 

Dropping into the debug console, here's what it says:
Browse[1]> widths
[1] 0.9 0.9 0.9 0.9 0.9 0.9 0.9 0.9 0.9
Browse[1]> range(widths)
[1] 0.9 0.9
Browse[1]> diff(range(widths))
[1] 2.842171e-14
Browse[1]> zero_range(range(widths))
[1] FALSE

It should be returning TRUE here. So it does look like there's a precision problem, but I think the only consequence of it is that you get a warning. I'd suggest conducting a more precise test to make sure that's the case, though.

-Winston
